defect_observations.observation: Precision (not a coverage verdict): 'if c=0, a smaller size can attain the same power' holds only when P0(L>0)<alpha. If P0(L>0)=alpha (e.g. f0 uniform on [0,1], f1 uniform on [0,alpha]) then c=0 and every power-1 test has size at least alpha; annex lines 102-105 show only that the size constraint is slack, not that a strictly smaller size exists.

The sum-band probability 1-(1-Delta/theta)^2 silently replaces the held source's (47) P=1-(Delta/theta)^2 (Neyman 1937 p. 357). The handbook's band is the correct one (simulation: at alpha=0.95 the source's printed band has coverage about 0.397); this is the root of the C001 and C003 gaps. C002 itself asserts only the displayed systems' coverage and is judged covered.

The held source's (93)-(94) (p. 369) put the switch line x1=theta1/2 in the upper branch and use the strict bound x2<alpha(theta1-x1). With those literal conventions the inverted set is half-open when x2/x1<alpha and empty on the positive-probability wedge alpha<=x2/x1<1-alpha when alpha<1/2, contrary to the source's 'may serve as regions of acceptance'. The handbook's completion repairs this and is flagged as 'required' (lines 12-13, 227-228), so C010/C011 are judged covered, but the source's own convention and its failure are not recorded.

Proposition X's hypothesis (3) (a boundary point with positive density) and the source's proof route via the pointwise threshold (105)-(111) are not recorded; the entry gives a strengthened variant described as 'underlying' Proposition X, which matches the component description.
Apparatus: 'The normal transformation theorem' is invoked without a cross-reference; thm:p15-normal-sums (handbook/parts/p15/convolution-gamma-normal.tex:314) is the matching entry.
